description: Retirement registry. Each entry is a capability this product retired, the ruling that retired it, and a concrete signature checkable against LIVE state (database or cluster) -- never a repo grep. A repo-only check reports clean even when a shared migration or a shared container image reinstates the capability outside this repo's control, which has already happened twice (see scripts/governance/check-retirement-registry.mjs header). Signatures are keyed to the product that retired them; a signature is only ever evaluated against that product.

entries.ruling: Guild-war sync retired; replaced by manual upload (job 149).
entries.rulingSource: job 149 (ticket ruling). Quoted verbatim in supabase/migrations/20260920010000_ps516_drop_guild_war_sync_columns.sql and supabase/migrations/20260925030000_ps516_drop_guild_war_sync_machinery.sql, which retire the DB-side remnants; this registry entry was the first place it was written down.

signatures.description: any of the five retired guild_config war-sync state columns present on the shared General database. A later migration dropped them; before that drop the row-value signature was `SELECT count(*) ... WHERE war_sync_enabled = true` (19 rows in the original ticket, 17 at the refreshed review). Once the column is gone that query ERRORS, which this gate reports as `could not reach live state` rather than as a clean retirement, so the signature is now the columns themselves -- a strictly stronger one: a shared migration that re-adds the column is caught even before it sets a row true.
signatures.detect: SELECT count(*) FROM information_schema.columns WHERE table_schema = 'public' AND table_name = 'guild_config' AND column_name IN ('war_sync_enabled', 'consecutive_war_sync_failures', 'last_war_sync_error_at', 'last_war_sync_error_reason', 'last_war_sync_error_details')

signatures.description: any dead guild-war-sync table reappearing on the shared General database; the manual guild-war upload tables are deliberately not listed
signatures.detect: SELECT table_name FROM information_schema.tables WHERE table_schema = 'public' AND table_name = ANY($1)

entries.ruling: The pre-modular historical backfill queue processor (edge function process-backfill-queue) retired. It called two RPCs -- process_historical_backfill_queue and complete_historical_backfill_queue_item -- that no migration in this repository's history ever created, over a historical_backfill_queue table that likewise never existed here, and it fanned out to /functions/v1/historical-backfill, an edge function that is not in this repository and is not routable by the edge runtime's VALID_FUNCTIONS. No pg_cron schedule and no application code invoked it. The surviving path is historical-backfill-modular, which is both cron-scheduled and invoked from app/lib/jobs.
entries.rulingSource: operator ruling; the edge function was removed from this repository

openQuestions: Competitive Intel and captured-replay-surface signatures above are table names read directly out of the DROP TABLE lists in the 2026-09-03 retirement migrations. That is strong live-checkable evidence, but neither migration cites an edge-function name or cluster deployment the way guild-war-sync does -- if either capability also had a dedicated edge function, this registry does not yet cover it. Flagging as open rather than guessing a function name.

The original 'job 149' ruling for guild-war sync is ticket-only; the migration that dropped the war-sync columns now quotes its text ("TA has no guild war syncing. Only manual uploads.") in-repo. If job 149 has a canonical write-up elsewhere, its source should replace 'job 149 (ticket ruling)' here.
